items.title: Manjung council seizes 17 fighting cocks from house
items.summary: LUMUT: Seventeen chickens believed to be used for cockfighting were seized from a house in Resident 3, Bandar Baru Setia Awan Perdana (BBSAP), here, yesterday. Manjung Municipal Council (MPM) Licensing and Enforcement Department director Mohamad Sharil Salihan said the council had previously issued a notice ordering the homeowner to clean up the premises. MPM therefore took enforcement action and seized the chickens believed to have been used for cockfighting," he said here today.

items.title: Fadhlina: 691 teachers need immediate psychological intervention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 691 teachers need immediate psychological interventions following a nationwide screening of 82,126 educators by the Education Ministry. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Psychological Well-Being Inventory (IKPsi) findings showed 636 teachers were at a moderate level, 32 at a moderately low level, and 23 at a low level. However, she said the vast majority, or 99.16 per cent, recorded good psychological well-being, comprising 50,869 teachers at a high level and 30,566 at a moderately high level.

items.title: Anwar expresses deep sadness, extends condolences to Spain after deadly train collision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed deep grief over the tragic loss of lives in the train collision in Spain. In a Facebook post, he said however Malaysia stood in solidarity with the people of Spain at this difficult time. “On behalf of the Government and people of Malaysia, I extend our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the Government and people of Spain, and especially to the families of the victims,” prime minister said.

items.title: Petroleum subsidies projected to hit RM40bil this year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's petroleum subsidy bill is projected to reach RM40 billion this year as a global supply crisis pushes crude oil prices above US$120 per barrel. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said monthly subsidies for petrol, diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) surged from about RM800 million in January and February to nearly RM5 billion in March and April. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had adopted a balanced approach to protect Malaysians from rising fuel prices while safeguarding the country's fiscal sustainability.

items.title: Anwar warns decline in reading and shallow thinking threaten civilisation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The decline of reading culture and the rise of shallow thinking in the digital age are pressing challenges that could threaten the future of civilisation, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post yesterday, the prime minister shared his thoughts after taking time to read the latest work by James Marriott, titled The New Dark Ages: The End of Reading and the Dawn of a Post-Literate Society . The question, therefore, is not merely whether humanity still reads, but whether humanity still wants to think,” he said.

items.title: Singapore, Indonesia leaders hold high-level talks amid bilateral challenges
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto have held high-level talks amid recent bilateral challenges. Singapore Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan said the communication had established political commitment on both sides to do "what is necessary", and that the focus was now on implementing and executing the plans and commitments. The transcript of the interview was made available by Singapore's Foreign Ministry.

items.title: New bridge to end Pulau Bruit's ferry dependence, ushering in economic revival
items.summary: SIBU: The new Batang Paloh Bridge, a RM289.8 million project opening tomorrow, will end Pulau Bruit, Daro's reliance on ferries and mark a new chapter in the island's economic growth. Deputy Premier of Sarawak and Minister of Infrastructure and Port Development Sarawak Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas announced the bridge's opening at a recent sitting of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly. He said the Batang Paloh Bridge, together with the completed Muara Lassa Bridge, will strengthen the coastal road network and enhance Pulau Bruit's connectivity with Daro, Tanjung Manis, Sarikei and surrounding areas.

items.title: Adam Adli: PH, Bersatu may clash in Melaka polls
items.summary: Melaka PKR acting state chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said clashes could occur in seats beyond the seven PH has decided not to contest. Adam Adli, who is also PKR communications director, said the coalition's decision to contest only 21 of the 28 state legislative assembly seats did not mean it deliberately vacated the remaining seven to make way for Bersatu. We decided to contest 21 seats because that matches our current capability.

items.title: CTOS faces weaker Q4 earnings on cyber disruption, higher taxes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd is expected to report weaker fourth-quarter earnings as cybersecurity-related service disruptions and higher tax expenses weigh on profitability, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. Analyst Mohd Shanaz Noor Azam said the temporary suspension of selected credit reporting services following the incident in late September could affect about 35 per cent of the company's revenue. Shanaz said the expiry of CTOS's tax incentive on Nov 8 would add to earnings pressure, with taxable income becoming subject to the statutory corporate tax rate of 24 per cent.

items.title: PN banks on local, professional candidates for Melaka polls
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional is confident that its candidates for the Melaka election, scheduled to be announced tonight, can secure voters' support. PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the line-up comprises individuals from diverse backgrounds, including locals and professionals who are active in community work. Commenting on which party will contest the most state legislative assembly seats, Tuan Ibrahim said the matter would only be confirmed after the official announcement.

items.title: Malaysia faces population decline as fertility rate continues to fall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's total fertility rate (TFR) remains below the replacement level, recording 1.6 children per woman aged 15 to 49 in 2024. National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN) director-general Datuk Abdul Shukur Abdullah said the rate was well below the population replacement level of 2.1 children per woman. "This rate is far below the population replacement level, which is around 2.1 children per woman," he said.

items.title: Govt reaches 1.65 million people in Malaysia through Info on Wheels programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Information Department (Japen) has implemented the Info On Wheels (IOW) programme at 23,962 locations nationwide, reaching an audience of 1.65 million from January 1 to September 23, in an effort to expand the dissemination of information related to the Madani Government’s policies, assistance and initiatives. The Communications Ministry said that 5,571 JIWA@Komuniti Madani: Sembang Santai programmes were also implemented during the same period, involving 616,961 members of the Madani Community to enhance public understanding of various government initiatives. The ministry answered Suhaizan Kaiat’s (PH-Pulai) question regarding the government’s communication strategy in addressing the public’s confusion about government policies and benefits, which makes them easily influenced by false information and propaganda.

items.title: Orange economy state-level meeting expected in November, Fahmi says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A meeting involving state executive councillors (Exco members) to discuss developments in the orange economy is expected to be held in the third week of November or by the end of the month, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the proposed working committee would involve state Exco members and ministers to discuss the progress of the orange economy in their respective states. Fahmi said the government needed time to obtain feedback from state governments before the Orange Economy Council met again.

items.title: Magnitude 5.5 quake hits Japan's Chiba Prefecture
items.summary: TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.5 struck the northeastern part of Chiba Prefecture, near Tokyo, early Thursday, Kyodo News reported, citing the country's weather agency. The quake, which occurred at 12.07am local time and measured lower 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, originated at a depth of about 52 kilometres and posed no tsunami threat, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency. The quake was also felt in Tokyo and neighbouring prefectures, including Tochigi, Ibaraki and Saitama.

items.title: PM Anwar expresses deep sadness over the tragic train collision in Spain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed deep grief over the tragic loss of lives in the train collision in Spain. In a Facebook post, he said Malaysia stood in solidarity with the people of Spain at this difficult time. "On behalf of the government and people of Malaysia, I extend our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the government and people of Spain, and especially to the families of the victims," Prime Minister said.

items.title: Umno confirms pact with PAS, Perikatan for Melaka polls, to launch joint manifesto
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Umno has confirmed its political cooperation with PAS and Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th Melaka state election, which will include a joint election manifesto between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN. Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was made at the party’s supreme council meeting yesterday. He said Umno had directed all its election machinery and supporters to give their full backing to PN candidates contesting in the state election.

items.title: Sabah, Sarawak rural road funding has not been cancelled, says minister
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Allegations regarding the cancellation or reduction of allocations for the rural road projects (JALB) in Sabah and Sarawak by the Madani Government need to be examined based on accurate facts and information, said the Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. “The fact is, the original allocation for JALB at the national level continues to increase from RM2.11 billion for the year 2026 to RM2.27 billion for the year 2027, compared to the previous era which never reached RM1 billion before Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration initiated an allocation of RM1.09 billion in 2023. Mustapha said the federal government’s continued commitment to the development of the Borneo region is reflected in Budget 2027, which allocates RM18.7 billion to Sabah compared to RM17.6 billion previously, while the allocation for Sarawak is increased from RM15.1 billion to RM16.2 billion.

items.title: Pakatan sticks to 21-seat target for Melaka polls for now, Fahmi says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is maintaining its decision to contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election for now, with any changes subject to a final decision by the coalition’s top leadership. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the coalition will concentrate on the seats that have already been announced. “We have announced 21 seats.

items.title: Melaka BN resolves seat dispute with MCA ahead of state polls, Ab Rauf says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The seat allocation issue within Barisan Nasional (BN) involving component party MCA for the upcoming Melaka state election has been resolved, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. “MCA is okay, settled. Commenting on matters discussed during the meeting, Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said party machinery had been directed to focus election work on the 21 state seats BN is contesting.

items.title: Bersih questions Loke's RM1,000 taxi aid announcement ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (Bersih) has criticised Transport Minister Anthony Loke for announcing a RM1,000 special financial assistance for taxi drivers during a Pakatan Harapan candidate announcement event for the Melaka election. The Bersih steering committee said the move could create the perception that the aid was a contribution from a contesting party, even though it was funded by government revenue. It said government-funded assistance should not be announced or promoted at political campaign events, as it could provide an unfair advantage to the ruling party.

items.title: Police seize 376kg of pangolin scales worth RM376,200 in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Police detained three local men and seized 376.2kg of pangolin scales worth an estimated RM376,200 in an integrated operation at a premises in Negeri Sembilan on Tuesday. In a statement yesterday, Bukit Aman WCB/PSK JKDNKA Commander SAC Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said police found 15 boxes of pangolin scales during a search of the premises, suspected to be linked to the storage and distribution of products derived from protected wildlife. Mohd Zaki said the case was being investigated under Section 68 of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), relating to offences involving wildlife, its parts or derivatives.

items.title: MACC probe into KWAP’s eFishery investment ongoing, Finance Ministry says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is still investigating Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) investment in Indonesian aquaculture technology company eFishery, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said yesterday. KWAP has also cooperated with relevant authorities and the investor consortium in taking appropriate action against those responsible, MoF added. Tuan Kalam also requested clarification on the investment approval, the parties responsible for the due diligence failure, total losses, and whether KWAP will take action against the negligent, MoF said.

items.title: Rice smuggling bid foiled in Gua Musang: 25 tonnes of Thai rice seized, driver held over dubious invoices
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 29 — The General Operations Force (GOF) has seized a lorry carrying 25 metric tonnes of Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled in from Thailand, during an operation in Paloh here last night. GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said personnel on patrol spotted a suspicious lorry near Kampung Pangkal Senor, along the Kota Bharu-Gua Musang highway. “The inspection found that the lorry was carrying Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand.

items.title: Foreigner arrested over alleged assault on auxiliary policeman at Genting casino
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 29 — A foreign national has been arrested for allegedly injuring an auxiliary police officer and damaging casino equipment at Sky Casino in Genting Highlands, Bentong, on Tuesday. Acting Bentong district police chief DSP Azmi Mahmod said preliminary investigations revealed that the 34-year-old man, believed to have been drunk, had allegedly behaved aggressively towards members of the public before entering the casino. Azmi said the officer had since received treatment at Bentong Hospital.

items.title: Fallen trees hit six vehicles in Selangor, no casualties reported
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the first incident occurred at Jalan MR 1/6, Rawang, at 4.40pm, when a tree belonging to the Selayang Municipal Council fell onto three vehicles. A team from the Batu Arang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 4.54 pm, with four personnel and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) deployed,” he said in a statement yesterday. A team from the Puchong Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 5.14pm.

items.title: AI literacy, BRICS participation among focus of Dewan Rakyat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry's plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) literacy into the school curriculum, Malaysia's participation as a BRICS partner country and the drafting of an AI Governance Bill are among the key topics to be addressed in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on the Parliament website, during Ministers' Question Time, Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok) will ask the Education Minister to outline the ministry's plans to incorporate AI literacy into the school curriculum through the AI Literacy Guide. The winding-up session for the debate on the Supply Bill 2027, scheduled for tomorrow, will involve several ministries, including the Plantation and Commodities Ministry, the Communications Ministry, the Human Resources Ministry, the Economy Ministry, the Youth and Sports Ministry and the Finance Ministry, before the Dewan Rakyat proceeds to vote on the Bill.

items.title: Malaysia records 3,581 child abuse cases in first half of 2026
items.summary: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) said 1,522 cases were recorded in the first quarter (January to March), with the number rising to 2,059 in the second quarter (April to June). KPWKM also highlighted an upward trend in cases involving child neglect and abandonment during the same period. “JKM recorded 987 cases of abandonment, including child neglect, in the first quarter of 2026.

items.title: Jawi introduces multi-tier graves to optimise cemetery space [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Territory Islamic Religious Department (Jawi) has introduced tiered burials at the Raudhatul Sakinah Islamic Cemetery in Kepong to optimise limited burial space. The pilot project is being implemented by the department's Mosque Management Division in collaboration with the Dakwah Management Division and the Kuala Lumpur Public Works Department (PWD), specifically for unclaimed bodies. Jawi said the initiative also introduces a pulley machine developed by Kuala Lumpur PWD to lower bodies to a depth of eight feet.

items.title: Learn from Indonesia-Singapore gas row, build up own energy resources, maritime expert tells govt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Indonesia’s move to cut natural gas exports to Singapore should be a reminder for Malaysia to develop and maximise its own natural resources to strengthen energy security, according to a maritime industry player. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said countries must ensure that their natural resources and energy infrastructure support domestic needs and long-term economic interests. Indonesia began reducing natural gas exports to Singapore on Oct 24.

items.title: Newborn buried alive in Kapit in critical condition
items.summary: KAPIT, Oct 29 — A newborn baby boy was found buried alive near a rented house on Jalan Airport here on Tuesday. Kapit district police chief DSP Rohana Nanu said the baby was found by police officers after hearing its cries while conducting a search in the area. The newborn was found buried,” she said when contacted today.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: AI literacy, Brics role and AI Bill on the agenda
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Ministry of Education’s plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) literacy into the school curriculum, Malaysia’s participation as a Brics partner country, and the drafting of an AI Governance Bill are among the key topics set to be addressed in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper available on the Parliament website, during the Ministers’ Question Time, Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok) will ask the Minister of Education to outline the Ministry’s plans to incorporate AI literacy into the school curriculum through the AI Literacy Guide. The winding-up session for the debate on the Supply Bill 2027, scheduled for tomorrow, will involve several ministries including the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities, the Ministry of Communications, the Ministry of Human Resources, the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Youth and Sports, and the Ministry of Finance before the Dewan Rakyat proceeds to a vote to pass the Bill.

items.title: Perak SADC prioritises staff wellness
items.summary: IPOH: Perak State Agricultural Development Corp (Perak SADC) has strengthened its workplace health culture through the Perak SADC Active & Wellness Day 2026 programme. Perak SADC chief executive officer Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusof said untreated health problems could affect employees' ability to perform their duties effectively and, in turn, impact organisational productivity. "Sometimes, we see even young employees facing health problems.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar on expectations of OPR normalisation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by the possibility of overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation at Bank Negara Malaysia Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting next week. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0720/0800 against the US dollar from Wednesday's close of 4.0745/0790. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the unchanged OPR at 2.75 per cent could provide support for the local currency.

items.title: Nike deepens India push with new running shoe, seeking fresh growth engines
items.summary: NEW YORK: Nike unveiled on Wednesday its first-ever running shoe designed specifically for India, marking the sportswear giant's latest bid to reach shoppers in the world's most populous country as it grapples with a sales slump in other key regions including China. The shoe, dubbed Vegam Run, follows Nike's announcement earlier this month that it plans to open a new campus in India, where it is seeking to make inroads amid a running boom. It was developed in about five months, Nike said.

items.title: 25 tonnes of suspected Thai smuggled rice seized in Kelantan
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 25 tonnes of white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand along Jalan Bentong-Kota Bharu near Paloh here on Tuesday night. Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said an inspection found that the lorry was carrying white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand. "The lorry driver produced two copies of invoices to explain the source and destination of the rice consignment.

items.title: Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes kill five
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Gaza's civil defence agency and a local hospital said Israeli strikes killed five people and wounded others in the Palestinian territory on Wednesday. The local hospital said it had received three bodies and 15 wounded people, one of whom later died from his injuries, according to Gaza's civil defence agency. Gaza's civil defence agency said another person was killed in a strike in Khan Younis, also in the south.

items.title: Early savings pave the way for a child's future
items.summary: A CHILD'S future is full of possibilities. Many children start developing their ambitions and dreams young. For parents, preparing for their children's future is not something that can be achieved overnight.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher as Fed holds key rate steady, focus turns to earnings
items.summary: NEW YORK: US stock indexes advanced on Wednesday after the US Federal Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected, leaving investors betting on a rate hike at its next monetary policy meeting in December. Financial markets are pricing in an 85.00 per cent likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December meeting, up from 78.30 per cent on Tuesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool. SK Hynix's US-listed shares jumped 13.30 per cent.

items.title: Dollar falls after Fed holds rates steady
items.summary: NEW YORK: The US dollar fell against major currencies on Wednesday after the Fed delivered a rate decision in line with expectations, while the New Zealand dollar fell sharply after that country's central bank surprised markets by leaving interest rates unchanged. The euro was up 0.32 per cent against the dollar at US$1.1160. Against the Japanese yen, the dollar was down 0.04 per cent at 157.87 yen.

items.title: Japan wants tougher action on cross-border threats
items.summary: BANGI: Japan called for stronger adherence to the rule of law and closer coordination among Asean countries to tackle cross-border threats, including maritime security challenges and transnational scam operations. Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki said Japan wanted to work with Malaysia and other regional partners to uphold a free and open international order based on the rule of law. Japan was also strengthening maritime security ties with Malaysia, including support for the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and cooperation between the countries' coast guards.

items.title: US Fed holds interest rates steady despite 'too high' inflation
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, even as its Chairman Kevin Warsh said inflation remained "too high" but insisted that politics played no part in the central bank's decision not to continue raising rates days before crucial midterm elections. The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 per cent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September. Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate quarter-point rate hike.

items.title: Corporate reputation as a strategic priority
items.summary: Safeguarding corporate reputation must therefore be a strategic priority for boards and senior management. Understanding Reputation Risk Reputation risk is the possibility that negative stakeholder perceptions will adversely affect an organisation's business operations, financial performance, market position or long-term sustainability. Common Sources of Reputation Risk Several factors threaten corporate reputation.

items.title: Data centres must secure water, power supply before approval [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Data centre investments must have adequate water and electricity supplies before they can receive federal government approval, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said the government would ensure that states have sufficient water supplies to support data centre developments without compromising the needs of other industries. "When it comes to water supply, we will ensure the state government is committed to securing sufficient water supply.

items.title: Malaysia must turn US$50bil AI investment into high-value jobs, technology gains [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must turn a proposed US$50 billion (RM204 billion) investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres by a global investor into higher-paying jobs, technology transfer and stronger local businesses, rather than simply expanding its digital infrastructure, economists say. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on Saturday that Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia had been identified as locations for the proposed investment. Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the proposed investment could boost economic growth, create skilled jobs and expand opportunities for local suppliers.

items.title: ECERDC beats target with RM10.3bil investments in 10 months [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Economic Region Development Council (ECERDC) has exceeded its 2026 investment target, recording RM10.3 billion in realised investments in the first 10 months, or 104 per cent of its RM10 billion annual goal. ECERDC also secured RM13.2 billion in committed investments, above its RM10 billion target. Terengganu led all states with RM4.8 billion in realised investments.

items.title: UKM law faculty breaks into global top 100
items.summary: BANGI: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) Faculty of Law entered the global top 100 for the first time, ranking 99th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings by Subject 2026. UKM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Sufian Jusoh announced the achievement at the opening of the Tuanku Chancellor International Conference on Law 2026 (TCC 2026) here yesterday. It brings together academics, policymakers, legal practitioners and researchers to examine the rule of law and good governance amid increasingly complex global challenges.

items.title: Leak website releases data on tens of thousands of DHS employees
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it had released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence. DHS did not respond to multiple messages seeking comment. The disclosure — which the non-profit data transparency group said drew on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" — is the third major government data leak to make headlines in the past month.

items.title: Inside KL’s SMART Tunnel: The hidden work behind its flood-fighting operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — On a daily basis, motorists driving through the motorway section of Kuala Lumpur’s SMART Tunnel may pass through without giving much thought to the two gates that remain shut beyond the familiar stretch of road. Yet behind those gates lies another side of the tunnel — never seen by motorists. Only about 3km of the tunnel doubles as a motorway.

items.title: A road when it’s dry, a river when it pours: How KL’s SMART Tunnel switches from highway to flood channel
items.summary: The 9.7km Stormwater Management and Road Tunnel combines a 3km double-deck motorway with a flood-control system designed to divert excess water away from the city centre during heavy rain. Why was the SMART Tunnel built? The 9.7km-long floodwater tunnel that channels floodwater to the Taman Desa holding pond.

items.title: Malaysia’s latest haze cost RM8b in welfare losses, may have led to 1,700 deaths, report finds
items.summary: The haze also disrupted manufacturers indirectly through staff absences and school closures. Among 59 sites reporting some operational impact in FMM’s survey, 81 per cent said they experienced more sick leave or health-related absence, while 63 per cent said school closures affected staff availability. School closures during the haze affected an estimated 8.4 million to 13.4 million student-days, the report said.

items.title: FMM report: Haze cost some Malaysian firms about RM280,000 in masks, medical expenses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The recent haze has cost some Malaysian businesses additional haze-related expenses of at least RM280,000, according to a report commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM). The report said 45 sites provided estimates of extra spending in FMM’s survey of 86 member sites, 81 of them manufacturers. Masks were cited by 76 per cent and medical costs by 58 per cent, the report said.

items.title: Appeal court imposes 20-year sentence on headmaster for child sex offences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today sentenced a headmaster to 20 years in jail and 11 strokes of the cane for making pornography and committing physical sexual assault against a standard six student five years ago. A three-judge panel, chaired by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin alongside Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dismissed Anuar Kintan’s appeal against his conviction and sentence of nine years and eight strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court for the charge of making pornography. The court subsequently convicted him of the charge, sentencing him to 11 years with three strokes of the cane.

items.title: PM says Budget 2027 reinforces Islam, criticises ‘hypocrite’ accusation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that Budget 2027 was formulated to continue promoting Islam, including through specific measures to strengthen pondok religious schools nationwide. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government had sought the views of Islamic scholars and religious teachers in drawing up the budget to ensure that the development needs of Islam received due attention. Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan; and Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.

items.title: High Court dismisses ex-Axis adviser’s appeal, upholds jail term and RM800,000 fine
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The High Court here today dismissed the appeal by former Axis Incorporation Bhd board adviser Lee Koon Huat against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abetting the furnishing of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia. “The High Court further agreed with the SC’s submission that the sentence imposed against Lee was appropriate in view of Lee’s role in the commission of the offences. “As such, the court dismissed Lee’s appeal against sentence and upheld the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court, being six months’ imprisonment and a fine of RM200,000 for each charge or in default, six months’ imprisonment,” it said.

items.title: Anwar: Dialogue with Myanmar offers best hope for Rohingya solution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia has opted for diplomacy in dealing with the refugee issue involving Myanmar, despite facing international criticism over the government’s approach to resolving the matter, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the approach was necessary to seek a solution after years of criticism and condemnation directed at Myanmar had failed to bring about any significant change in the country’s policies. “When I invited Myanmar President (Min Aung Hlaing), what was the objective?

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia must embrace AI, quantum technology without losing cultural roots
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia must continue to master emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing, to remain competitive globally while preserving its religious and cultural identity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said technological advancement was essential to ensuring the country kept pace with global developments, but must be anchored in religious faith, moral values, culture and literature. Our faith, morals, values, culture and literature,” he said.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: More stringent checks at KLIA to combat drug smuggling
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — More stringent inspections are set to be implemented at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) following an increase in reported drug smuggling cases at the nation’s primary gateway, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry will also be identifying ‘blind spot’ areas that are not monitored by close circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the KLIA 1 and 2 terminals. He said both KLIA 1 and 2 have 5,000 operational CCTV cameras, but said there are still ‘blind spot’ areas.

items.title: Malaysia to deploy latest body scanners at RTS Link border checkpoint
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Latest technology scanners will be deployed at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Bukit Chagar here once the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link starts operations early next year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the implementation of this technology marks a first for Malaysia and serves as part of efforts to enhance security at the nation’s entry points. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail (left) presenting a memento to his Singapore counterpart Sim Ann, who is the Second Minister for Home Affairs, at the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (FTX 2026) closing ceremony at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site Johor Bahru today, Oct 28, 2026.

items.title: Ex-convicts among nine arrested in Miri grave desecration probe
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Police have arrested nine men believed to be involved in grave desecration activities in the Miri district during a special operation from October 11 to 17. Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said investigations revealed that three of the suspects had prior criminal records. "Following our action and investigations, police have solved 15 reported grave desecration cases in the Miri district.

items.title: Man remanded over Facebook caricature allegedly insulting police
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 — Police have arrested a 50-year-old local man in connection with an investigation into a caricature allegedly insulting the police that went viral on social media. In a statement today, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the 50-year-old self-employed man was detained outside Menara Seri Wilayah P2a in Putrajaya yesterday. Adzli said police had seized a mobile phone believed to have been used to make the post.
